headline: Your temple podcast went up with the title “What the Evidence Actually Say”, which names nothing people search: put Richard Eaton and the temples back in it today. The Churchill Short is due on 30 November with no script on disk, and the Sati Short, already written, takes the slot the lapsed Tegh Bahadur Short left.

top3.topic: 14 December 1971: the killing of Bengal's intellectuals
top3.signal: Sixteen days out; the research step falls on 30 November and nothing is scripted. The channel's 1971 Short “1971 War: Operation Cactus Lily | Meghna Heli Bridge” is one of its five best Shorts for subscribers per view.
top3.recommendation: On 30 November find who drew up the list and who carried it out, with names and the date. Script a Short of about two minutes for the morning of 14 December, the culprit in sentence one, and judge it on day three.

top3.topic: 6 December: the Vishnu-Hari slab from the Babri rubble
top3.signal: Eight days out. Your second Irfan Habib Short, on the slab that came out of the rubble on 6 December 1992 and the museum stone he said it was, is written and waiting for your edit.
top3.recommendation: Edit it this week and record it in the same sitting as the Sati Short. Publish the morning of 6 December with “Vishnu Hari inscription” in the title, the searched name, and pin links between it and the first Habib Short. The first one earned little, so the date's lift is a guess.

top3.signal: Nineteen days out; the research step falls on 3 December.
top3.recommendation: From 3 December, check what Timur's own memoir says about the prisoners killed before the battle. If it holds, a Short for the morning of 17 December that opens on his words. The channel's earlier Timur Short brought no subscribers, so this is a guess.

skipped.topic: Three films on 4 December: Maatrubhumi, Eetha, Baba
skipped.signal: All three open on 4 December. The radar finds no confirmed history subject for any of them, and Baba's subject is unverified.
skipped.recommendation: Skip unless a trailer shows one is about a figure in the channel's lane. Do not script from headlines.

skipped.signal: Guru Nanak's English Wikipedia readership is 8.05x its usual, 9,365 a day.
skipped.recommendation: Skip. A saint's life is one of the kinds of Short the channel's own checks turn down, and this week has three dated Shorts already.

whats_working: “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” is this month's best subscriber-earner: 3.9 net per 1,000 views on 127,500 views, and long-form views rose 24.8% week over week. Long-form was 4 of the 23 uploads in the last 30 days, yet over 28 days it earned 87.7% of the net subscribers videos brought.

The best subscriber-earner of the last 90 days is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, 12.9 net per 1,000 views, and over the 365-day window it is “The Church That Ran Britain's PRISON Camps”, 34.3. Both put a colonial-era culprit on trial with its own records. The Churchill and Sati Shorts are built the same way.
The podcast's first day: 4,751 views in 27 hours, and the most-liked comments ask for more like it. Day one is the subscriber test; judge it on 30 November by engaged views and subscribers.
whats_wrong: Since yesterday the podcast's title went from “Did Hindus Kings Loot Temples?” to “What the Evidence Actually Say”: no question, no name, and a missing s. Long-form is found on Home (270,430 long-form views over 28 days came through Home and the subscriptions feed, against 7,957 from search), where the title is most of what a viewer sees. Probable cause of a slow second day, if it comes: nobody can tell what it is about. Test: retitle today and compare views an hour on 30 November with today's 174.6.

Shorts views fell 63.9% week over week (19,524 against 54,051), and the three newest with data brought next to no subscribers: 0, 1.1 and 0 per 1,000 views. Probable cause: the Ramayana film Shorts have aged, and none of the newer ones rode a date or a release. Test: the Churchill and Sati Shorts each ride a date; judge both on day three against these three.

Two dated Shorts lapsed in five days with nothing made, and neither open decision has a script on disk. Probable cause: dated Shorts are being chosen with less time than writing, recording and editing take. Test: if the Sati Short, written since September, ships on 4 December and the unwritten Churchill one does not, choose dated Shorts only from scripts already on disk a week ahead.

Long-form views overstate real viewing: only 41.5% of November's long-form views were engaged views, and over the 365-day window long-form now brings 7.1 subscribers per 1,000 views, below the range it used to hold. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing, which YouTube has counted as views since August. Test: judge the podcast and the Bali video by engaged views and subscribers, never by views.

actions.action: Retitle the podcast. “What the Evidence Actually Say” could read “Did Hindu Kings Loot Temples? Richard Eaton vs the Inscriptions”.
actions.rationale: Its own description opens with that question and names Eaton, and those are the words a searcher types. It has 4,751 views so far, so few have seen the current title.

actions.action: Set the Related video of today's Short, “Richard Eaton Says Hindu Kings DESTROYED Temples”, to the podcast, and pin the podcast's link in its comments.
actions.rationale: The Short is the podcast's way in. Whether a Short sends viewers on is a guess, but the link takes a minute.

actions.action: Upload the Malay Ravana Short to YouTube with its Related video set to the Indonesia long-form.
actions.rationale: Written since 19 November and still not on YouTube, while the Indonesia long-form keeps bringing subscribers every day.

actions.action: Answer the theology objections under the podcast with sources (/replies drafts them).
actions.rationale: They are the only disputes so far; answered, they protect the inscription chapters the Shorts will be cut from.

growth.verdict: Needs 223 net subscribers a day. The channel does 71.04/day, so the target is a **3.1x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "1. Current rate, nothing changes"), reaches 71/day — still 3.1x short. At that ceiling rate 100,000 arrives on 2030-01-19, 3.1 years out.

scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1282 of the 3,355 subscribers that 22 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 31.8/day (891 of 1,847 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 22 long-form and 105 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.5 more long-form videos a year — 39.5 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 33 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 153, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 448 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 31.8/day (891 of 1,847 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 9 revision long-form videos, median 69 subscribers, against 33 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 31.8/day (891 of 1,847 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,282 subscribers on 73,183 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
